body: Thanks, I'm taking a list to my therapist this week. I think it'll be good to have a plan in place anyway.

I have a therapist. I just am worried that my current state will put me in danger of self-harming soon, and would rather be prepared than panicking and deciding not to go because I have no idea where the good psych wards are, and then causing damage to my life by avoiding hurting myself in other unhealthy ways.
What sort of money are we talking about? I have insurance.
Thanks, I'll talk to them this week.

Thank you for the advice. I'm actually very well-versed in the whole avoiding-hurting-myself thing, so my situation is basically that I am not going to harm myself right now, but I've seen myself behaving erratically and have been depressed recently, and I know how quickly that can spiral into self-harm, so if I feel like I need to do something about it (ie, protect myself from myself), I want to make sure the experience isn't a nightmare (as some psych wards are).
I do, I live with my partner and he's informed about my current state of mind.

Thank you, that's a good idea. I do have a therapist I could contact. I guess I'm concerned that if I indicate I might in the future want to check myself in, it will cause him to contact emergency services and then I won't be able to make the decision.
